landing.subtitle: An immersive visualisation of climate threats weighing on Pacific islands — rising seas, cyclones, coastal erosion, coral reef bleaching.
landing.section1_body: Météo-France's cyclone database records every track since 1960. Analysis reveals a marked intensification of events since the 2000s, with record pressure spikes and wind speeds.
landing.section2_body: In the event of a centennial cyclone, OBLIC data reveal storm surge levels potentially reaching several metres in certain coastal sectors of New Caledonia. Thousands of people live in these risk zones.
landing.section3_body: The Coral Reef Observation Network (RORC) continuously monitors the health of reef ecosystems. Coral bleaching, accelerated by ocean warming, threatens the unique biodiversity of the Caledonian lagoon.

guide.label: Documentation · Cyclone data
guide.title: Reading guide
guide.sub: Understanding South Pacific cyclone data — classification, fields, interpretation and sources.
guide.intro_intensity: Cyclonic phenomena in the South-West Pacific are classified into 7 intensity levels, defined by the maximum 10-minute average wind speed and minimum central pressure.
guide.intro_fields: Each database record contains 16 fields for positions and 20 fields for trajectories. Here are the main fields and their interpretation.
guide.intro_faq: Frequently asked questions about interpreting cyclone data.
guide.intro_sources: The data used in this visualisation come from official open sources, in accordance with the Pacific Dataviz Challenge 2026 requirements.
guide.source1_desc: History of each phenomenon's position every 6h since 1977/1978. Produced by Météo-France New Caledonia.
guide.source2_desc: Complete trajectories of 212 events with global characteristics (max intensity, start/end dates, minimum pressure).
guide.source3_desc: South Pacific Enhanced Archive of Tropical Cyclones. International reference database enriched by Météo-France for the NC zone.
guide.source4_desc: All data are published under Open Licence v2.0 (CC BY equivalent). They can be freely reused, modified and shared with attribution.
guide.source4_cite: Citation: SPEArTC (Diamond, H.J., A.M. Lorrey, K.R. Knapp, and D.H. Levinson, 2012), Météo-France, Weather and Climate Service of the Government of New Caledonia.
